# T21 model results (generated by `t21_race.py`)

Generated by `python t21_race.py grid`. Run time 525 s, peak memory 539 MB, numpy 2.5.3. All numbers are percentages unless stated.
P(attack) is the probability, under the attacker's best play, that Bob's claim is not final when the public tip
reaches the deadline D (so that Alice keeps both legs). Model and assumptions: `docs/miner-concentration.md`, section 2.
`S` = blocks between the reveal and D; `*` marks the span at the latest allowed reveal: guaranteed (planning rate, 20 s per
block) and typical (30.3 s per block). Clean start = no private lead at the reveal; rho = 2; depth cap 18 (final at 19).
Tie rules: **strict** = a tie is never published (a lower bound); **free** = at equal length she publishes a tie that wins
with probability 1/2 and costs nothing when it loses (she sees both hashes first); **always** = every tie she publishes
wins (an upper bound). `lead L` = she starts with L private blocks (a = L, d = 0). `wait` = optimal stopping: she may
delay the reveal for the real swap timeline (production 377 public blocks, sepolia 170; derivation in the report).
Values below 0.0001 % are printed as `<0.0001`; the CSV has the full numbers.

## 4. Standard error of a measured share

A share measured over N blocks has standard error sqrt(q (1 - q) / N) (blocks treated as independent draws).

| N blocks | q = 0.30 | q = 0.40 | q = 0.45 | q = 0.50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 720 | 1.71 (2 sigma 3.42) | 1.83 (2 sigma 3.65) | 1.85 (2 sigma 3.71) | 1.86 (2 sigma 3.73) |
| 2880 | 0.85 (2 sigma 1.71) | 0.91 (2 sigma 1.83) | 0.93 (2 sigma 1.85) | 0.93 (2 sigma 1.86) |
| 20160 | 0.32 (2 sigma 0.65) | 0.35 (2 sigma 0.69) | 0.35 (2 sigma 0.70) | 0.35 (2 sigma 0.70) |

(Standard error and 2 sigma in percentage points.) Hashrate drift inside a swap is not included.

## 6. Re-send delay rho (block events from a removal until the claim is back), strict tie

rho = 2 is the base case. Bob's tool re-sends within one tick (30 s) of noticing; the rotation guard (the last 4 blocks before
each 144-block epoch boundary), a pending close by Alice, and an operator who must run the spending step by hand all make
rho larger. Larger rho favours the attacker.
